marks.gloss_en: these are those for which one does not slaughter, neither in the Temple nor in the country: a white spot [in the eye]
and a tumtum and an androginos -- neither in the Temple nor in the country
דכתיב ״ויהי שחין פורח אבעבועות באדם״ (Shemot 9:10) -- kind svara, the nearest kind for the stam's own proof-verse

אלא, תלתא הוו: דקרא -- יבש מבפנים ומבחוץ; דמתניתין -- לח מבחוץ ומבפנים; דמצרים -- יבש מבפנים ולח מבחוץ (= p_garav_dekra, p_garav_dematnitin, p_garav_demitzrayim; that this answers 41a.9 by assigning the incurable garav to Egypt's is the author's reading, header)
the stam: rather, there are three: the verse's [garav] -- dry both inside and outside

וגרב לא? והכתיב ״גרב״ באורייתא! -- and garav is not [a blemish]? but 'garav' is written in the Torah! (kind svara: no kind names a verse contradiction, header). Still standing after the first answer: אלא גרב אגרב קשיא (41a.8)
וחזזית לא? והכתיב ״ילפת״ באורייתא! ותניא: ילפת -- זו חזזית המצרית
the stam: garav is written in the Torah [among the blemishes]
גרב אגרב נמי לא קשיא, הא בלח, הא ביבש. לח -- איתסי, יבש -- לא מיתסי (= p_ha_belach_ha_beyavesh, p_lach_mitrapeh)
בשלמא חזזית אחזזית לא קשיא: כאן בחזזית המצרית, כאן בחזזית דעלמא (= p_kan_mitzrit_kan_dealma)
the stam: here [the verse] the Egyptian chazazit, there [the mishnah] an ordinary chazazit
ולח מיתסי? והכתיב ... ״ובחרס״ ... ״אשר לא תוכל להרפא״! (kind svara: a verse contradiction, header)

the stam: Devarim 28:27 'the Lord will smite you with the boil of Egypt ... and with garav and with cheres'; since it writes 'and with cheres', 'garav' there states the moist kind -- and it says 'from which you cannot be healed'
a baraita: [it is] the upper joint
״או חרוץ או שבור״ -- חרוץ דומיא דשבור: מה שבור במקום עצם, אף חרוץ במקום עצם
אמר קרא או חרוץ או שבור -- חרוץ דומיא דשבור, במקום עצם (= p_abaye_charutz_bimkom_etzem)
Abaye: the verse says 'or cracked or broken' -- cracked is like broken: as broken is in a place of bone, so cracked is in a place of bone
מנא הני מילי? דתנו רבנן: מן הבהמה -- להוציא רובע ונרבע (kind svara is the nearest: no kind names a baraita adduced as source, header)
מן הבקר -- להוציא את הנעבד
מן הצאן -- להוציא את המוקצה
ומן הצאן -- להוציא את הנוגח
the baraita: 'from the animal' -- to exclude one that copulated with a person and one that was the object of bestiality
כיון דאמר גרב זהו חרס -- from the baraita's identification of garav as cheres
דכתיב ומראהו עמוק מן העור -- the proof-verse for its being a crack (kind svara: a sage's own proof-verse)
בלא שבור נמי ... כתב רחמנא גרב למימר דחרוץ במקום בשר לא הוי מומא (= p_rava_charutz_basar_eino_mum, p_rava_garav_melamed)
Rava: even without [the comparison to] 'broken' you cannot say that a crack in a place of flesh is a blemish
הני בני קטלא נינהו! -- these [the rovea, nirva and the gorer] are liable to death; why does a verse exclude them from the altar?
על פי עד אחד או על פי הבעלים -- [known] by one witness or by the owner, so it is not put to death
אלא במדינה נמי, נהי דזכר הוא -- תעשה נקבות חריץ, וישחוט עלה! -- in the country, even granting it is male, let its femaleness be a crack (חריץ) and let him slaughter on account of it
the stam: the androginos -- granted not in the Temple, for perhaps it is female
the stam: granted the tumtum -- not in the Temple, for perhaps it is female; not in the country, for perhaps it is male and has no blemish
(entertained) then the Merciful One could write 'cracked' and not need 'garav', and I would say: cracked, which is not repulsive, is a blemish -- garav, which is repulsive, not all the more so?
the stam, for R' Yishmael: perhaps [Rava's rule holds] where it is not noticeable; but where it is noticeable we call it 'an ill blemish'
for these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn
and [the tanna] states it anonymously over all of them -- including the blemishes taught in the names of individuals
מנהני מילי? דתנו רבנן: ״מן הצאן ומן הכשבים ומן העזים״ -- פרט לזקן ולחולה ולמזוהם (kind svara is the nearest: no kind names a baraita adduced as source, header)
the baraita: 'from the flock, from the sheep and from the goats' (Vayikra 1:10) -- to exclude the old, the sick and the foul-smelling
the stam: and they are necessary: had the Merciful One written [an exclusion] for the old, which does not become healthy again -- the sick, which does become healthy again, say [it is] not [excluded]
the stam: and had the Merciful One written two, [to exclude] these that are weak -- the foul-smelling, which is not weak, say [it is] not [excluded]
